rotations.name: Continuous rice (current practice)
rotations.rationale: Rice was the dominant crop in 11 of 12 years (USDA CDL, 2014-2025), so this is the comparison point.
benefits: Heavy, poorly drained clay suits flooded rice
risks: High water use: about 811 mm May-Oct evapotranspiration in rice years (OpenET, single-pixel estimate)
No break in rice pest and weed cycles
The site was 97.53% fallow in 2022 (CDL); the cause is not in our data
info_gaps: Crop trait scores are illustrative (0-10) and need local agronomic review
No farm-level cost or price data
Why the site was fallow in 2022 is not measured

rotations.name: Rice then winter wheat
rotations.rationale: A winter small grain in the off year needs less irrigation water than rice and adds a different crop family.
benefits: Lower irrigation need in the wheat year
Breaks rice weed and pest cycles
risks: Willows soils (92.0% of the site) are poorly drained silty clay, which can waterlog non-rice crops (SSURGO)
info_gaps: Crop trait scores are illustrative (0-10) and need local agronomic review
Crop scores are averaged across the sequence (simplification)

rotations.name: Rice then soybean or dry bean
rotations.rationale: A legume in the off year can fix nitrogen and give a different income stream.
risks: Willows soils (92.0% of the site) are poorly drained silty clay, which can waterlog non-rice crops (SSURGO)
Needs summer irrigation and different equipment
info_gaps: Crop trait scores are illustrative (0-10) and need local agronomic review
Crop scores are averaged across the sequence (simplification)

rotations.name: Rice then safflower
rotations.rationale: A low-water, deep-rooted oilseed in the off year reduces water use and breaks rice pest cycles.
benefits: Much lower water need in the safflower year
risks: Willows soils (92.0% of the site) are poorly drained silty clay, which can waterlog non-rice crops (SSURGO)
info_gaps: Crop trait scores are illustrative (0-10) and need local agronomic review
